minutes.headline: Ag Commission approved June and July minutes, deferred officer elections, and set a Sept. 10 special meeting on a farm-complaints letter.
minutes.summary: The Agricultural Commission met remotely with three new members. It approved two sets of minutes by roll call and postponed reorganizing officers until a missing member could join. Much of the evening went to who handles farm complaints and inspections. A member read a draft letter to town officials, and the commission agreed to try for a special meeting two weeks out.

what_happened.line: The Agricultural Commission approved its June and July minutes by roll call at a remote meeting with three new members.
Members agreed by poll to try for a September 10 special meeting on a letter about who handles farm complaints; the chair will request it.
A draft letter to town officials on farm complaints and inspections was read, and members are to send comments to the chair, who will compile them.
Election of chair, vice chair and clerk was postponed until the missing member joins or the end of the meeting.
The chair will try to book Zoom meetings for September through December, and a commission Facebook page was requested for a future agenda.

why_it_matters: Where a farm complaint or inspection request is sent, and who answers it, affects both farmers and neighbors; the letter proposes to settle that between several town offices.
The commission has no elected officers yet, so its letter and meeting requests rest on the chair acting before a reorganization vote.
